newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sidek outlook bleak, standstill continues.
newsitem.headline: Sidek outlook bleak, standstill continues.

text.p: The outlook for Mexico's Grupo Sidek continues to worsen as the debt-ridden holding company has again postponed a financial restructuring plan, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I still think it is possible the company will cease to exist," said Bond Snodgrass, equity analyst at the Mexico City-based Arka brokerage. "I really think the outlook is still bleak."

Sidek requested that its creditors grant another extension to a standstill agreement, which expired Nov 29, to June 30, 1997, the company informed the Mexican Stock Exchange on Tuesday. The new request "is postponing the inevitable, which is basically that the company cannot pay its debts and that it will not be able to pay its debts next year, either," Snodgrass said.

Extending the standstill until June 1997 would be tantamount to saying the financial restructuring plan will not be unveiled until then, said Deyanira Becerra, equity analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
"Uncertainty in the company is huge, and I do not see the share price gaining," Becerra said.

Sidek series B shares were trading at 66 centavos at mid-session on Tuesday, compared with 3.50 pesos on Jan 2, 1996, and 13.94 pesos on Dec 19, 1994, when a sudden devaluation of the peso plunged the Mexican economy into its worst recession in seven decades.
"The company has not paid interest since February 1996, which the creditor banks are obviously accruing. All that is happening is that the debt is growing, as most of it is in dollars," she said.

On several occasions, Sidek CEO Luis Rebollar has said delays in unveiling a debt restructuring plan have been due to a lack of consensus among foreign creditors, as Sidek seeks to continue as a going concern after selling off assets.

Santiago Pique, an analyst with Bear Stearns in New York said, "they haven't found a way to reduce the debt to levels they want and at the same time still have enough assets to continue as a going concern."
Whereas Abaco and Inverlat have a sell recommendation for Sidek stock, Bear Stearns recommends holding while waiting for it to rebound.
Grupo Sidek was not available for comment on the request to extend the standstill.
